videos.title: Why the Spider Sees the Moon #Shorts

comments.author: @olgarohner7907
comments.text: From a universe perspective we are not too much bigger than spiders... We can see stars...
comments.replyText: That is such a beautiful way to think about it. We really are not that different when you look at it from a cosmic scale. Both of us looking up at the same moon, just from very different sizes of existence. Really grateful you took something thoughtful from this one.

comments.author: @NiVRO90
comments.text: How do we know? Also wtf is up with this video?
comments.replyText: Great question. Scientists discovered this by studying the jumping spider retina under electron microscopes. They found four distinct layers of photoreceptor cells, each sensitive to different wavelengths of light. Behavioral tests confirmed they can distinguish the moon from stars by having them look at different light sources. As for the video style, it is a new format we are trying with stock footage and narration. Always looking to improve.

clipCandidates.momentLabel: Brain smaller than poppy seed sees the moon
clipCandidates.why: The emotional punchline — a creature with a brain smaller than a poppy seed can look up at the night sky and see what we see. Strong curiosity gap and shareable.

videos.title: Why the Iguana Has a Third Eye #Shorts

clipCandidates.why: The mechanism — parietal eye detects shadow shifts in milliseconds, triggers a reflex to flee before the brain processes the threat. Counterintuitive survival system.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: Why an iguana runs from a shadow it never even sees

videos.title: Why the Seal Survives 5000 Feet Underwater #Shorts

clipCandidates.why: The extreme physiological shutdown — heart rate drops from 90 to 4 bpm while running on reserve oxygen a mile underwater. Most shocking stat in the video.
clipCandidates.hookRewrite: Why a seal's heart beats only 4 times per minute underwater
